summary: At segment 0 step 40, the h input selects the wished scroll of taming. C enters read.c:seffect_taming() and maybe_tame() for the adjacent hostile grid bug; its first unmatched RNG draw is the consumed resistance check rn2(108)=23 in zap.c:resist(). JavaScript still has note_unported("read.c seffect_taming") in its seffects() dispatch, so it skips the effect and reaches a different rn2(12)=11 draw at the aligned index. The active missing owner is read.c:maybe_tame/seffect_taming, not zap.c:resist; js/zap.js:resist and js/dog.js:tamedog already implement those dependencies. The remaining source task is the complete taming effect/helper port and replacement of the dispatch gap.

source.branch: For SCR_TAMING or SPE_CHARM_MONSTER, seffects() calls seffect_taming(). In the selected case the wished scroll is not cursed, the hero is not confused or swallowed, and an adjacent hostile grid bug is in range. seffect_taming() calls maybe_tame(), which consumes resist()’s boolean before deciding whether to call tamedog(); it then aggregates changed/visible candidates and updates the scroll-known flag from the visible result.
callers: C: read.c:doread() invokes seffects(scroll) at read.c:635; seffects() dispatches SCR_TAMING and SPE_CHARM_MONSTER to seffect_taming(&sobj) at read.c:2236-2238. The selected command path is the recorded r/read action, followed by h selecting the wished scroll from inventory.

JavaScript: js/read.js:doread() calls seffects(scroll, state) at line 882; js/read.js:seffects() currently handles SCR_TAMING and SPE_CHARM_MONSTER with note_unported("read.c seffect_taming") at lines 1509-1512.
dependencies: read.c:maybe_tame() consumes zap.c:resist(mtmp, sobj->oclass, 0, NOTELL) at line 1056; the existing implementation is js/zap.js:resist(), whose SCROLL_CLASS attack level is 9 and whose rn2 bound is 100 + alev - dlev.

read.c:maybe_tame() discards dog.c:tamedog()’s return value at line 1057; the existing stateful implementation is js/dog.js:tamedog(). C still requires awaiting its messages and mutations when wiring the effect.

The cursed arm calls mon.c:setmangry() and consumes its resulting peacefulness change, while the effect uses monst.c:m_at(), display.h:canspotmon(), and the hero’s swallowed/steed state. Existing JS counterparts include js/mon.js:setmangry(), js/monst.js:m_at(), and js/startup_a11y.js:canSpotMonster().

evidence: The exact current queue entry in /tmp/A24-main-workqueue.json records 2 remaining screens and 42 recorded steps for synthetic/v8/read-taming-scroll-hostile-monster. It points to challenges/evaluations/20260927093229-v8.json evaluated at 043629bb13447062cadb766644b34c3490bb9bde; the case remains 40/42 screens, 2546/2552 RNG values, and 41/42 cursors matched, with first mismatch at segment 0 step 40 on h.

The first C-side unmatched draw is rng index 2545, rn2(108)=23, annotated resist(zap.c:6141); the same input’s JS aligned draw is rn2(12)=11. The source annotation names the callee whose return is consumed, while the missing caller branch is visible directly in js/read.js:1509-1512 as note_unported("read.c seffect_taming").

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:1042-1063 defines maybe_tame(): cursed scrolls call setmangry(); otherwise C consumes resist()’s result and invokes tamedog() if unresisted or the target is a shopkeeper, then returns whether peaceful/tame state changed.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:1678-1719 defines the whole seffect_taming() loop. It handles swallowed heroes separately; otherwise it scans a radius of one (five when confused), includes a steed at the hero square, counts candidates, aggregates maybe_tame() results and visible results, prints the appropriate neighborhood message, and sets gk.known only for positive visible results.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:2191-2240 dispatches SCR_TAMING and SPE_CHARM_MONSTER to seffect_taming(). In JavaScript the source-order caller already exists as js/read.js:1441 and doread() calls it at line 882; only the two taming switch arms remain explicit gaps.

The source dependency behavior is already present at js/zap.js:1718-1746 (resist) and js/dog.js:229-250 (tamedog); the matching state/visibility helpers are in js/mon.js, js/monst.js, and js/startup_a11y.js. The missing call path therefore belongs in read.c’s taming helper/effect rather than a change to zap.c:resist.
